$comment: PLACEHOLDER RECORDS — subscriptions and the installments that settle them. A subscription is RECORDED (renamed from activated, 2026-08-31): the INVOICE is what entitles the customer, and recording writes down a sale that already happened. It still goes live immediately. Replaced by GET /admin/finance/subscriptions and GET /admin/finance/subscriptions/{id}. THE INSTALLMENT IS THE UNIT THAT GETS PAID, not the subscription and not a part of one: one installment, one payment, in full, and Σ of a subscription's installment amounts equals its totalPaise exactly. There is no part-payment field because there is no part-paid installment to record it against. `due` is the absence of an event, not a claim about one; `fail_to_pay` is evidence — a gateway response, or a due date that passed with nothing against it — and it carries that evidence in `failure`. Every payment below is a row that already exists in the money-in ledger, carrying the same paymentId, amount, mode, reference, value date and account; where `bankLineId` names a statement line, the amount and the reference on that line are the same ones written here. `bankLineId: null` means the money is real and the statement covering it has not been imported yet — normal, not a defect. Integer paise throughout. The clock is asOf 2026-08-25T09:00:00+05:30, and the only dates after it are `endDate`, which is where the service term runs to, and the `dueDate` of a `due` installment, which is the whole point of one.

subscriptions.$comment_installments: The duplicate charge is modelled as ONE subscription with ONE installment, not two of either. Farah agreed to pay ₹35,400 once, so the schedule holds one installment; her card was then charged twice inside two minutes on 16 Aug — PAY-4399 (pay_QK8s21bvC, invoice 00079) and PAY-4400 (pay_QK8s21bvD, invoice 00080), same amount, same token. A duplicate charge is two payments, not two subscriptions and not two installments, so the second charge stays where it belongs: a row of its own in the ledger, with RF-0117 raised against PAY-4399 to send one of the two back. The subscription is `active`, not `refunded` — she keeps the plan, and PAY-4400 is the charge that pays for it.

subscriptions.$comment_installments: The gateway decline. AutoGrowth is charged monthly against a card mandate, so the first installment was attempted the moment the mandate was registered and the issuer refused it twice. Nothing was invoiced — the sales chain raises the invoice when the installment is collected, so `invoiceNumber` is null and stays null until a charge succeeds. `failure` carries what the gateway actually returned, not a summary of it. Installments 2 and 3 are `due`: their dates have not arrived, nothing has been attempted against them, and a failed installment 1 says nothing about them.

IB-INV-2026-00085 carries the label 'Pro' in its description because the catalogue renamed that tier to Scale in June and an invoice is frozen at issue: the document keeps the name it was raised with.

They are all in CLOSED PAST MONTHS (2025-09 to 2026-06) and every one is terminal — completed subscriptions, recorded transactions — so the reporting period (August 2026) is byte-identical with or without them: active count, MRR, collection rate, the tax summary and every August figure are untouched.
